blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The House prosecution panel rejected suggestions of a compromise that would convict Vice President Sara Z. Duterte in her Senate impeachment trial while leaving her eligible to seek public office, calling the idea unconstitutional. Speaking to reporters, House private prosecutor and legal spokesperson Atty. Benjamin “Jay” Tolosa Jr. emphasized that the Constitution strictly dictates the consequences of a conviction. “That has no basis, and it’s inconsistent with the provisions of the Constitution, which provides that if an impeachable officer is found guilty… then she should suffer the penalties of removal from office and perpetual disqualification,” Tolosa stressed.
